label: Eric Burlison
narrative: Burlison is the member who took the disclosure fight off the witness table and onto the contractors. He arrived at the July 2023 hearing an announced skeptic - 'I have been here for 6 months and I am pretty skeptical... I am from Missouri. You have got to show me' - and used his round to test whether the recovered material could be domestic, which Grusch denied. He then radicalised on the process rather than the phenomenon. In March 2024 he led a bipartisan call for a House select committee on UAP focused first on the money, and said flatly that DoD lied to members in a classified setting: 'They weren't transparent to us in a SCIF setting. So they could have brought forward evidence. They could have explained what these Special Access Programs actually do. But they are not willing to do that with Congress.' In March 2025 he hired David Grusch as a senior adviser on UAP matters for a four-month term - the whistleblower moving inside the legislative branch. At the 9 September 2025 hearing he publicly unveiled, for the first time, footage he says shows an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at an orb off Yemen on 30 October 2024, and put two further stonewalls on the record: that his UAP disclosure amendment to the NDAA had been ruled non-germane 'mostly deemed by staff, not even an elected official,' and that in 2024 'we were blocked by someone in House administration from being able to receive a full briefing from AARO.' In 2026 he turned the investigation onto the FFRDC layer, writing MIT Lincoln Laboratory in May 2026 for a classified 1952 'flying saucer talk' briefing recording (their attorneys agreed to comply within 30 days) and MITRE on 22 May 2026 with a ten-page demand covering over forty production categories and records back to 1930. His stated theory: 'If you really want to hide something from Congress, you don't put it in a government file cabinet. You hand it to a private contractor. That's why my investigation is following the trail into RAND, MITRE, Aerospace Corp, MIT Lincoln Labs, and the Northrop Grummans of the world.' In April 2026 he and Chairman Comer opened the congressional probe into the deaths and disappearances of scientists tied to sensitive research, triggered by the vanishing of retired Air Force Gen. William Neil McCasland.
